channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Veja situações onde Moraes vê que Flávio desrespeitou ordens judiciais
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes identified two episodes in which Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) allegedly violated judicial orders related to the imprisonment of former President Jair Bolsonaro. The most recent occurred on July 11, 2025, when Flávio disseminated on social media a letter written by his father during an authorized visit, breaching the purpose of the visitation right. The earlier episode took place on August 3, 2025, when Flávio posted a video featuring Jair Bolsonaro participating by phone in a Copacabana beach protest, violating a precautionary measure banning the former president from using social media directly or through third parties; the post was later deleted following public backlash.

item.title: Deputado bolsonarista é condenado a pagar R$ 15 mil ao PT
item.description: Federal deputy Paulo Bilynskyj (PL-SP) was sentenced by Brasília’s 2nd Civil Court to pay R$ 15,000 in damages to the Workers’ Party (PT) for falsely linking the party to drug trafficking in social media posts. The court ruled the statements exceeded legitimate political debate and constituted civil wrongdoing, rejecting his claim of parliamentary immunity. Bilynskyj said he will appeal, calling the ruling political persecution.

item.title: Damares sai em defesa de Michelle Bolsonaro e chama apoiadores que as atacam de ‘aloprados’
item.description: Senator Damares Alves (Republicanos-DF) defended former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro during a Senate speech, calling 'crazy' the right-wing voters and allies attacking them for allegedly abandoning pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro. She denounced the attacks as political gender violence, cited false accusations of having a lover, and said the Senate’s legal office will help her file a representation against those involved, though she does not know who is behind the campaign.

item.title: Lula defende taxa sobre exportação de petróleo para segurar preços
item.description: President Lula defended the continuation of a 12% tax on crude oil exports, stating that the additional revenue is being used to subsidize fuels and curb domestic prices amid international market volatility driven by Middle East conflicts and U.S.-Iran tensions. The tax, extended for at least two more months via a Gecex/Camex resolution, has backing from government officials including Alckmin and Boulos, though oil companies oppose it, arguing it undermines market expectations and their prior plans for its removal following falling oil prices.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio diz que decisão do STF de suspender visita é ‘autoritária’
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign criticized a decision by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes that banned the senator from visiting his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, for 90 days after Flávio shared a handwritten letter from Jair on social media. The campaign called the ruling authoritarian, disproportionate, and a political interference, claiming it aims to isolate the ex-president and reflects political persecution. Moraes ruled that the letter constituted an illegal early campaign appeal, violating house arrest conditions banning social media use, and referred the matter to the Electoral Prosecutor's Office for investigation.

item.title: Os argumentos de Alexandre de Moraes para suspender visitas de Flávio a Bolsonaro por 90 dias
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes suspended Flávio Bolsonaro's right to visit his imprisoned father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, for 90 days after Flávio shared a letter from Bolsonaro on social media, violating a court order banning the ex-president from using social media directly or through intermediaries. The ban prevents visits until after the first round of the 2026 presidential election on October 4, based on the finding that Flávio misused his visitation rights and has repeatedly disregarded judicial decisions.

item.title: Governo Lula envia 48 toneladas de leite em pó a Cuba em meio a crise
item.description: The Lula government sent 48 tons of powdered milk to Cuba in two shipments: 16 tons departed from Canoas (RS) on Monday, and 32 tons are scheduled to leave Porto Alegre on Tuesday. The humanitarian aid was decided in a meeting with ministers and military officials, responding to Cuba's worsening supply crisis exacerbated by U.S. sanctions and frequent blackouts.

item.title: “Interferência no jogo político”, diz Marinho após Moraes suspender visitas de Flávio
item.description: Senate opposition leader Rogério Marinho (PL-RN) criticized Justice Alexandre de Moraes' decision to ban Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) from visiting his father for 90 days, calling it clear interference in the electoral process. Marinho claimed the move targets the Bolsonaro family and aims to undermine their 2026 campaign.

item.title: Figueiredo: bolsonarismo jogará Moraes na "lata de lixo da história"
item.description: Paulo Figueiredo criticized Minister Alexandre de Moraes' decision to suspend Flávio Bolsonaro's visits to his father, Jair Bolsonaro, for 90 days after the latter's letter endorsing the son's presidential candidacy was shared online. Figueiredo claimed Bolsonarism will survive and 'throw Moraes into the trash can of history'.

item.title: Lula manda recado para Ancelotti e alfineta jogadores que não voltaram ao Brasil
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized the few Brazilian national team players who returned to Brazil after the World Cup elimination, noting only Danilo, technical staff, and CBF officials came back on the chartered flight. He also jokingly suggested that coach Carlo Ancelotti hire a robot he saw at the Mauá Institute of Technology to win a future World Cup, comparing the robot to players like Mbappé and Haaland.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio diz que decisão de Moraes é "interferência no jogo político"
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's pre-campaign criticized Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes' decision to suspend Flávio's visits to his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, for 90 days after the disclosure of a letter written by Jair. The statement, signed by Senator Rogério Marinho, called the measure authoritarian, disproportionate, and political interference, claiming unequal treatment compared to Lula's access to communication during his imprisonment.

item.title: Oposição reage à decisão de Moraes contra Flávio e fala em perseguição
item.description: The decision by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes to suspend Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's visits to former President Jair Bolsonaro for 90 days prompted opposition lawmakers to denounce it as political persecution. PL members warned the move could influence the 2026 presidential race.

item.title: Marinho: proibição das visitas de Flávio a Bolsonaro afeta a campanha
item.description: Rogério Marinho, coordinator of Flávio Bolsonaro's pre-campaign, criticized Alexandre de Moraes' decision to ban Flávio from visiting jailed ex-president Jair Bolsonaro for 90 days, calling it arbitrary and damaging to the campaign. He argued the restriction is unconstitutional and inconsistent, noting Moraes had previously allowed Bolsonaro to give an interview while now blocking the reading of a letter.

item.title: Decisão de Moraes deixa Flávio sem visitar Bolsonaro até depois do 1º turno
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes suspended visits by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to former President Jair Bolsonaro, preventing direct contact between father and son until after the first round of the 2026 elections. The measure aims to prevent undue influence in the electoral process.

item.title: A tentativa de ex-deputados de reverter perda de mandato
item.description: Former deputies Paulão (PT-AL) and Dayany Bittencourt (União Brasil-CE) appealed to the STF to reverse the loss of their mandates, decided by the Chamber of Deputados following a vote recount in the 2022 federal elections ordered by the Electoral Justice. They argue their defense was not heard in the Chamber’s internal process and that the TSE has not yet issued a final ruling. The security filings were assigned to Ministers Cristiano Zanin (Paulão) and Luiz Fux (Bittencourt).

item.title: Dino suspende regra que dispensava eleição para presidência da Assembleia Legislativa do Amazonas
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino suspended a rule of the Amazonas Legislative Assembly that allowed the vice-president to assume the presidency without a new election in case of vacancy, ordering the application of the Chamber of Deputies' Internal Rule, which requires a new election within five sessions. The preliminary injunction will be submitted to the STF plenary between August 14 and 21, arising from an ADI filed by the Solidariedade party challenging succession changes in the Amazon's Executive and Legislative branches in 2026, including the April resignation of the governor and vice-governor and the indirect election of Roberto Cidade as governor in May.

item.title: Carlos Bolsonaro reage à decisão de Moraes e defende o irmão Flávio
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro reacted to a decision by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes that suspended for 90 days the visits of his brother Flávio Bolsonaro to former President Jair Bolsonaro, following the publication of a letter in which Jair expressed support for Flávio in a potential future presidential race. Carlos defended Flávio on social media, stating that despite opposition, 'it's Flávio Bolsonaro or the country is over'. Moraes also demanded clarification within 48 hours on whether Jair Bolsonaro violated the judicial order banning his use of social media, directly or through third parties.

item.title: Em semana decisiva sobre novas taxas dos EUA, Lula diz não acreditar em tarifaço
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said he does not believe in a 'tariff war' from the U.S. on Brazilian products, despite expectations of new 25% and 12.5% tariffs being announced by Wednesday. He noted the government is awaiting the decision to determine a possible response, considering tariff confirmation the most likely scenario, while negotiations aim to include exceptions. The comment was made during the inauguration of an ethanol-powered turbine in São José dos Campos, where he also advocated for strengthening Brazil’s defense industry.

item.title: Lula reclama da postura de jogadores da seleção após a eliminação
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized the conduct of the Brazilian national team players following their World Cup elimination, saying he had sent a message to coach Carlo Ancelotti. He made the remarks during a visit to the Mauá Institute of Technology in São Paulo, expressing disappointment with the team's performance.

item.title: Por decisão de Moraes, Flávio não poderá visitar Bolsonaro antes do 1º turno
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes has suspended Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's visits to his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, for 90 days, blocking contact until October 11 after Flávio shared a supportive letter from his father on social media. The disclosure violated a court order banning Jair Bolsonaro from using social media, who is currently under house arrest for a coup-related conviction. Moraes ordered Flávio's defense to explain within 48 hours whether Jair Bolsonaro knew about the letter's publication, citing potential judicial disobedience.

item.title: Brasil envia ajuda humanitária a Cuba
item.description: The Lula government has begun sending 48 tons of powdered milk to Cuba in two Brazilian Air Force flights, with the first departing from Canoas (RS) and the second scheduled to leave from Porto Alegre. The aid aims to address Cuba’s severe supply crisis, worsened by power outages and humanitarian hardship, and new donations of food and medicine are under evaluation. The operation followed a meeting between President Lula, ministers, and military representatives.

item.title: Os evangélicos são de direita?
item.description: A Datafolha survey reveals that 52% of Brazilian evangelicals identify with the right or center-right, compared to 43% of Catholics, but the article critiques the oversimplification of labeling evangelicals as 'right-wing'. It argues that the right has been more effective in translating its agenda into moral and religious language that resonates with evangelicals' lived experiences — such as violence, addiction, and family crisis — while the left relies on technical, institutional discourse that fails to connect with this group's symbolic world.

item.title: Com decisão de Moraes, Flávio Bolsonaro só verá o pai após 1º turno
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes suspended Flávio Bolsonaro's visits to his father, Jair Bolsonaro, for 90 days until October 11, 2026, after the senator shared a letter written by the former president on social media, violating the ban on Jair Bolsonaro's use of networks. The letter endorsed Flávio as a pre-candidate for the 2026 presidency. The decision prevents Flávio from seeing his father in person before the first round of the election on October 4.

item.title: Os filhos de Jair Karamazov ainda não desistiram de trancafiar o pai
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes barred Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting his father, Jair Bolsonaro, for 90 days after he violated judicial measures by using social media to disseminate a letter from the former president, constituting electoral crime and repeated disrespect for court rulings. The decision aims to prevent the Bolsonaro family from leveraging the gesture as a campaign tactic, given the letter’s clear intent to mobilize public support. Moraes emphasized the recidivist nature of the conduct, referencing a similar violation in August 2025.

item.title: Moraes apura propaganda eleitoral em vídeo de Flávio com carta de Jair
item.description: Justice Alexandre de Moraes suspended Flávio Bolsonaro's visitation rights to Jair Bolsonaro for 90 days after the senator released a video announcing he would read a letter written by the former president during house arrest. Moraes argued the letter's dissemination may violate the social media ban imposed on Jair Bolsonaro, either directly or through intermediaries, and ordered the defense to clarify whether the ex-president knew the letter would be made public.

item.title: Leia a íntegra de decisão de Moraes que suspendeu visitas de Flávio a Bolsonaro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes suspended for 90 days the visits of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest in Brasília. The decision followed Flávio's disclosure of a letter written by Bolsonaro reaffirming his pre-candidacy for the 2026 elections. Moraes also gave the defense 48 hours to explain the document's release and ordered the Electoral Public Prosecutor's Office to analyze whether premature electoral propaganda occurred.

item.title: Lula diz não querer guerra, mas fala em ampliar investimento em Defesa: 'Forças têm que estar preparadas para garantir soberania'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva advocated for increased investment in the Armed Forces to safeguard Brazil's territorial sovereignty, emphasizing the strategic importance of rare earths and critical minerals found in the country. He stated that military forces must be prepared to protect key resources, including oil beyond 200 nautical miles and seabed wealth, to prevent Brazil from remaining merely a raw material exporter. Lula clarified that he does not seek war, but insists Brazil must be highly prepared to defend its sovereignty amid global interest from powers such as the U.S., China, and Russia.

item.title: Decisão de Moraes é ‘absurda’ e impede Flávio de falar com pai até 1º turno, dizem aliados
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes barred Senator Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, for 90 days, preventing contact until the first round of the 2026 election on October 4. Allies of the PL campaign called the decision absurd and an undue interference in the former president's presidential bid.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro só poderá visitar o pai após o primeiro turno
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes has suspended visitation rights to former President Jair Bolsonaro for 90 days, preventing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting him before the first round of the 2026 elections. The ruling requires Bolsonaro’s defense to explain within 48 hours whether the former president knew in advance that a letter would be disclosed on social media by his son. The article is available exclusively to subscribers.

item.title: Moraes suspende visitas de Flávio e manda Jair Bolsonaro explicar envio de carta
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes suspended Flávio Bolsonaro's visits to his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, for 90 days and ordered the ex-president's defense to explain the sending of a letter read by the senator in a live broadcast, in which Jair designated him as his 'spokesperson' in the 2026 elections. Moraes understands that Flávio disrespected a precautionary measure by using his visitation right to disseminate political content on social media, constituting an abuse of purpose.

item.title: Críticas a Flávio Bolsonaro impulsionam Caiado nas redes, aponta levantamento da AP Exata
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado’s increased criticism of Flávio Bolsonaro led to a 446.3% surge in social media mentions over five days, according to AP Exata. Despite higher exposure, positive mentions dropped only 4.9 percentage points to 45.7%, showing image resilience. Caiado ranked second among presidential candidates in mention volume at 26.2%, behind Lula (34.3%) and ahead of Flávio Bolsonaro (25.6%).

item.title: Leia a íntegra da decisão que proíbe Flávio de visitar Bolsonaro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes suspended for 90 days the authorization for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to visit former President Jair Bolsonaro, after the senator shared on social media and in a video a letter written by his father, who is barred from using platforms directly or indirectly. The ruling was issued on Monday, July 13, 2026.

item.title: Ala do STF vê erro de Moraes ao questionar carta de Bolsonaro lida por Flávio
item.description: Supreme Court ministers believe Alexandre de Moraes erred by questioning the legitimacy of a letter written by Jair Bolsonaro and read by his son Flávio Bolsonaro. Three magistrates consulted by the column urged caution regarding any decision in this direction, warning of risks of judiciary politicization. The article is subscriber-only.

item.title: Carta de Bolsonaro renova duelo com Moraes e recoloca STF na campanha de Flávio
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro reignited his clash with Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes by sharing, on social media, a letter written by former President Jair Bolsonaro, violating STF orders that barred visits to his father for 90 days. The move aimed to prove to right-wing leaders threatening to abandon him that he has his father’s backing, solidifying his role as the sole spokesperson of bolsonarism amid internal competition with Michelle Bolsonaro. Simultaneously, the Bolsonaro clan used the episode to revive its narrative of persecution by the judiciary, shifting focus from internal power struggles and rumors of damaging revelations against Flávio in the pre-campaign phase.

item.title: Paulistas rejeitam privatizações de metrô e trem, segundo Datafolha
item.description: Datafolha poll reveals that a majority of São Paulo residents oppose privatization of the metro (56%) and CPTM trains (53%), with opposition rising significantly since 2023. There is also growing resistance to selling Santos Port (50%) and sustained opposition to Sabesp privatization (54%), despite many reporting no change in service. Electricity and toll roads saw declining public approval, while telecom and internet showed slight improvement.

item.title: Moraes proíbe Flávio de ter contato com Bolsonaro por 90 dias
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes barred Senator Flávio Bolsonaro from contacting former President Jair Bolsonaro for 90 days after the senator disseminated a letter attributed to the ex-president on social media, violating a judicial order that prohibits third-party communication. The measure aims to prevent Flávio from leveraging the message to boost his 2026 presidential pre-candidacy, which may constitute illegal early election campaigning.

item.title: Moraes proíbe visitas de Flávio a Bolsonaro por 90 dias
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes prohibited former President Jair Bolsonaro from receiving visits from Senator Flávio Bolsonaro during his house arrest for up to 90 days, until after the first round of the 2026 elections. The STF decision aims to safeguard the integrity of the electoral process and prevent potential pressures or interference amid Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential candidacy.

item.title: Crusoé: Lula classifica como ‘pirataria’ pedágio de Trump em Ormuz
item.description: President Lula (PT) labeled Donald Trump's announcement of a 20% 'toll' on oil shipments transiting the Strait of Hormuz as 'piracy.' Lula compared the move to historical maritime extortion, arguing Trump is using the pretext of clearing the route to profit from international trade.

item.title: Lula alfineta seleção brasileira após maioria dos jogadores não voltar ao Brasil: ‘Que vergonha’
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva harshly criticized the Brazilian national team after their loss to Norway in the World Cup, stating that only defender Danilo returned to Brazil on the team's flight, calling it a 'shame'. During a visit to the Mauá Institute of Technology, Lula also joked about a student-developed robot, suggesting that coach Carlo Ancelotti should hire it to improve the team's performance.

item.title: Moraes suspende visitas de Flávio a Jair Bolsonaro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes suspended visits by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest, for violating a judicial order banning social media posts and misusing visitation rights to disseminate a letter supporting Flávio’s presidential pre-candidacy. The decision followed a similar incident in August 2025 and prompted backlash from opposition and allies, with the PT filing a request to revoke Bolsonaro’s house arrest.

item.title: Moraes suspende visitas de Flávio Bolsonaro ao pai e manda apurar possível propaganda eleitoral antecipada
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes suspended Flávio Bolsonaro’s 90-day visitation rights to his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, after the senator shared a letter written by Bolsonaro during house arrest on social media, which Moraes deemed as potential early election campaigning and a violation of the ban on Bolsonaro’s use of digital platforms, directly or indirectly. The ruling also requires Bolsonaro’s defense to clarify within 48 hours whether he knew the letter would be published, and forwards the case to the Electoral Attorney General for investigation.

item.title: Bolsonaro usa metáfora sobre ângulos para falar de “soma de forças”
item.description: Lawyer João Henrique N. de Freitas reported that Jair Bolsonaro used a metaphor of mathematical angles — complementary (90°), supplementary (180°), and explementary (360°) — to advocate for unity and 'summing forces,' referencing a handwritten letter supporting his son, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, and emphasizing integrity and overcoming obstacles.

item.title: Moraes suspende visita de Flávio a Bolsonaro e dá 48h para explicar carta
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes suspended for 90 days the visits of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to former President Jair Bolsonaro after the latter’s alleged letter supporting Flávio’s 2026 presidential bid was shared on social media. The defense has 48 hours to explain the letter’s origin and authenticity.

item.title: Movimento Imparáveis nega ter sido criado por Michelle: "Inspiração"
item.description: The 'Imparáveis' movement denied being created by Michelle Bolsonaro, stating she is only its main inspirational figure. The note clarified that the movement was planned by former PL Mulher team members but was never formalized as an institutional project. Michelle remains affiliated solely with the Mulheres Conservadoras movement since 2024.

item.title: Advogada compara trabalhador que perdeu a mão com Lula e é repreendida
item.description: A lawyer was reprimanded by a labor prosecutor for comparing a worker’s hand amputation in a workplace accident to Lula’s severed finger in 1964, stating that pain cannot be compared. The 1st Panel of the TRT-23 unanimously upheld the company’s obligation to compensate the worker, rejecting the claim of exclusive worker fault.

item.title: The Economist: Pix ameaça domínio dos EUA no setor de pagamentos
item.description: The Economist article argues that Brazil’s Pix instant payment system challenges U.S. dominance in global payments, reflecting a broader trend of financial sovereignty as nations develop their own systems to reduce reliance on American firms like Visa and Mastercard. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer criticized Pix as harmful to American companies and proposed a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, but the Brazilian government, including Finance Minister Dario Durigan and President Lula, denies unfair competition, citing evidence provided to U.S. authorities. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro defended Pix against U.S. attacks but advised against linking it to international networks competing with American systems like Zelle.

item.title: Crusoé: Por que Lula caiu entre beneficiários do Bolsa Família
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll showed a 10-point drop in President Lula’s support among Bolsa Família beneficiaries, falling from 68% to 58% in first-round voting intention. This decline contrasts with rising support for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, though the exact increase is not specified in the text. The loss of confidence among social program beneficiaries may reflect dissatisfaction with economic management or perceived reduced effectiveness of the aid.

item.title: Governo registra baixo desempenho em metas da Saúde e do PAC, diz TCU
item.description: The TCU reported that the Lula administration underperformed in health and Novo PAC goals in 2025, achieving only 16.7% and 23.1% of targets, respectively, well below the overall average of 44.8%. Conversely, deforestation control and basic education exceeded the average at 53.5% and 58.3%. The court attributes the shortcomings to structural budget execution flaws and poor goal calibration, undermining public spending efficiency and strategic planning.

item.title: Lula diz que Brasil “não precisa morrer por conta do petróleo”
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Brazil does not need to rely on oil to survive and advocated for a transition to alternative fuels, emphasizing the need to 'fight' for the world to adopt a new energy model. He cited U.S. President Donald Trump as an example of someone who denies climate change and supported increasing the mandatory biodiesel blend in diesel from B15 to B17, a proposal submitted by biofuel sector entities.

item.title: Temporada de convenções: onde os presidenciáveis darão o pontapé inicial das campanhas
item.description: Presidential candidates for the 2026 elections have set the dates and locations for their official campaign launches during the party conventions period, running from July 20 to August 5. Most chose São Paulo as their launch site, including Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), Lula (PT), Renan Santos (Missão), and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), while Romeu Zema (Novo) is the exception, launching in Brasília. After the conventions, parties have until August 15 to register candidacies with the Electoral Justice.
